video.title: I Got Fired From My Job. Now I Make $450,000/year (Copy Me)

summary: David Heacock interviews Justin, who was fired from TGI Fridays and later from a commercial floor care firm, and now runs Midland Floor Care, a commercial floor care business in the DC area that did close to $450k last year. Justin started in residential cleaning with rented Home Depot equipment and bought leads, then moved into commercial work after asking a Massage Envy owner who did her floors. He grew through franchise referrals, and later through government contracts and bidding to prime contractors. The coaching half concludes his limiting factor is sales. David recommends hiring one proven salesperson from competitors or adjacent markets on a commission-heavy plan, building the sales financial model first, and incentivising contractors as partners.

ideas.name: Midland Floor Care: commercial floor care contractor
ideas.one_liner: Commercial floor maintenance, restoration and installation (polishing, strip and wax, carpet, wood refinishing, concrete polishing) for regional commercial buildings in the Washington DC area.
ideas.business_model: Recurring maintenance programs plus project work for commercial clients
ideas.customer: Office managers of health facilities, franchise owners (Massage Envy, European Wax Center), government buildings, prime contractors; buildings under 150,000 sq ft
ideas.problem: Commercial floors need ongoing appearance maintenance; buildings under 150k sq ft are underserved by large competitors

pricing.notes: Prices not stated; commercial payment terms net 30 to net 120.

acquisition_channels.details: Early residential leads bought from Service Magic / HomeAdvisor / Angi Leads.

quote.text: I found out about this uh this site that's now Angie's Leads, but it was it it was a couple different things
quote.speaker: Justin

acquisition_channels.details: First commercial client (Massage Envy franchise owner) referred him across her clinics and the franchise community.
Bidding on contractor portals PlanHub and BuildingConnected, then calling the GCs to ask about upcoming work and vendor requirements.
Website rebuilt by a marketer (Q) for SEO and automations: from about 2 calls a year to about 8 calls in 5-6 weeks.

ideas.delivery: Justin plus 3-4 full-time staff and part-time temp labour per project; started renting equipment from Home Depot.
ideas.startup_cost: Minimal: rented equipment from Home Depot, funded by temp work

acquisition.how: Portal bidding and SEO inbound can be partly automated; relationship selling to GCs is human. UK cold email to limited-company contractors is allowed under PECR.

billing.how: Invoicing automatable; long net terms need chasing.

uk_applicability.notes: Commercial floor care and contractor bidding portals exist in the UK; government contracts via UK procurement portals.

risks: Cash flow strain from net 30-120 terms

tactics.name: Ask every business you visit who does their floors
steps: Look at the floor wherever you go
Ask staff/owner 'who is doing your floors?'
Put the first client on a recurring program and follow them as they expand to more franchise units
Get referred within the franchise community

quote.text: Yo, who is doing your floors? Y'all this I can, you know, y'all need some help
quote.speaker: Justin

tactics.name: Prime contractor bidding to diversify
steps: Sign up on PlanHub and BuildingConnected
Bid on floor finishing/polishing packages
Collect GC contact info and call: anything else coming, are we in line as a vendor, what certifications do you need

quote.text: they have different like websites like planhub and building connected and all of that where signed up all all on those and um just bidding on contracts
quote.speaker: Justin

tactics.name: Use temp labour instead of fixed headcount
steps: Keep 3-4 core staff
Staff up per project via temp agencies so idle salaries aren't carried

tactics.name: Hire a first salesperson from competitors
steps: Network ~25% of your time to find someone already selling to your target customer
Look at competitors, adjacent markets (other cities) and adjacent products (flooring distributors)
Offer higher commission or bigger piece of the action
Commission-heavy structure, budget ~6 months of draw while they ramp
Do 90% of sales calls with them for the first 6 months
Or use independent reps on commission only

quote.text: I would find somebody that's working for one of your competitors and give them a opportunity to make more money
quote.speaker: David Heacock

tactics.name: Build the sales financial model before hiring
steps: Define pricing rules
Define commission structure aligned to margin (avoid reps underpricing)
Know delivery cost and margin
Set pipeline metrics: leads per week, follow-ups

tactics.name: Bootstrap equipment
steps: Do temp work for cash
Rent equipment from Home Depot for first jobs
Buy equipment from profits

warnings.warning: Big-name commercial clients may come with net 60-120 terms that strain cash flow.

quote.text: certain clients where it's like the name is so big you're like, you know what, ah that would look so great on my website

warnings.warning: Having most revenue tied to government contracts is concentration risk.

quote.text: I have a some government contracts where most of my business is tied up in that. So if anything was to happen I I'm I'm short
quote.speaker: Justin

warnings.warning: Being personable is not the same as being good at sales; owners avoid asking for the sale.

quote.text: being personable and being good at sales are two are two different things
quote.speaker: David Heacock

warnings.warning: Cutting residual commissions drove away good salespeople at his former employer.

quote.text: they did away with that and they they lost some they lost some good salespeople
quote.speaker: Justin

warnings.warning: Commission reps may price too low to earn commission while the business loses money.

quote.text: they're going to price too low. Um, and you're going to be sitting here and they're going to be getting their commission
quote.speaker: David Heacock

warnings.warning: Hiring someone just 'supposedly good at sales' is a mistake; hire someone who has sold to your customer.

quote.text: I don't want you to just go out and hire somebody >> that's supposedly good at sales
quote.speaker: David Heacock

lessons.lesson: Working inside an industry first, then starting your own firm in it, is a strong path.

quote.text: one of my favorite strategies for young people today is to go out, work for a business, learn it, and then go out and and um you know, do something entrepreneurial within it
quote.speaker: David Heacock

lessons.lesson: Being personable in customers' homes is rare and wins repeat business.

quote.text: most people are not personable
quote.speaker: Justin

lessons.lesson: Target the underserved mid-size segment big competitors ignore.
Small owners can't afford the best people, so they must be best at sales themselves until they can.

quote.text: until you get the resources, you're going to have to be the best
quote.speaker: David Heacock

lessons.lesson: Identify the limiting factor (here sales, not delivery) and take the highest-leverage action on it.
Prove a sales hire works once before scaling the sales team.

quote.text: Once you prove it works once, then you can then you can start doing it
quote.speaker: David Heacock

lessons.lesson: The answer is in doing, not in another course or podcast.

quote.text: you keep looking for the next solution when really the answer is in the doing
quote.speaker: David Heacock

lessons.lesson: Turn adjacent players (contractors, reps) into incentivised partners to multiply your sales force.
Variable temp labour keeps risk low in project-based service work.
A performance-focused website can turn a near-dead inbound channel into steady calls.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand operator story with a revenue figure but few unit economics; much of the episode is coaching advice.
